blocks.content: llama.cpp is the engineering practice used to run quantized language models efficiently on local and edge hardware.

Run quantized language models efficiently on local and edge hardware. In production, the hard part is not a single successful demo; it is building a contract that remains observable, secure, testable, and predictable under real traffic.

blocks.title: Core mental model
blocks.content: Model format, quantization level, context length, and hardware offload determine the real experience.
1. What llama.cpp Solves

llama.cpp belongs inside a wider AI system. It receives a defined input, performs one bounded responsibility, and produces an output that the next stage can validate. Keeping that boundary explicit prevents prompts, provider behavior, and business logic from becoming one fragile block.

["Define the user or system outcome before choosing llama.cpp.","Write down the input contract, output contract, latency target, and failure behavior.","Separate probabilistic model decisions from deterministic validation and side effects.","Keep provenance so outputs can be traced to inputs, model configuration, and tool results."]

Write down the input contract, output contract, latency target, and failure behavior.
Separate probabilistic model decisions from deterministic validation and side effects.
Keep provenance so outputs can be traced to inputs, model configuration, and tool results.

blocks.content: 2. End-to-End Architecture
A production llama.cpp implementation is a pipeline. Each stage should be independently measurable and replaceable.

blocks.title: Boundary rule
blocks.content: Every external response and model-generated structure must be validated before it enters trusted application logic.

blocks.content: The example keeps the orchestration small and pushes validation, policy, storage, and execution into explicit services. This makes unit tests possible and prevents a provider SDK from becoming the architecture.
4. Production Failure Modes

["Using llama.cpp without a measurable success criterion.","Allowing unbounded input, context, output, retries, or tool calls.","Assuming a valid JSON shape also means the action is authorized or correct.","Hiding provider errors behind generic retries until latency and cost explode.","Shipping without representative offline tests and production traces."]

Allowing unbounded input, context, output, retries, or tool calls.
Assuming a valid JSON shape also means the action is authorized or correct.
Hiding provider errors behind generic retries until latency and cost explode.

blocks.title: Least authority
blocks.content: Give the model the minimum context and the minimum set of capabilities required for the current request. Capability discovery must never silently become capability authorization.

blocks.content: llama.cpp is production-ready when its behavior is bounded, measurable, recoverable, and safe—not merely when the happy-path demo works.
